headline: Govt to bring Benazir Ahmed back from UAE for trial
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed assures Parliament that no leniency will be shown in bringing back fugitive fugitives, including former IGP Benazir Ahmed, to face justice.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated in the National Parliament on Tuesday that the government will show no leniency in bringing fugitive suspects, including Benazir Ahmed, back to Bangladesh to face trial.
The Home Minister noted that the government is coordinating with Interpol and various diplomatic missions to ensure the extradition of those currently residing abroad.

Benazir Ahmed, a former Inspector General of Police (IGP), served as the Dhaka Metropolitan Police Commissioner during the operations at Shapla Chattar. He faces allegations of enforced disappearances, corruption, and illegal asset accumulation.
Following the mass uprising of 2024, Benazir Ahmed left the country. Reports of his detention in Dubai have recently sparked demands in Parliament for his immediate return and legal action.

Members of Parliament from various parties, including Jamaat-e-Islami and BNP, called for strong measures to bring him back, with some proposing the creation of a special cell to identify and extradite fugitives.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kabir mentioned that extradition efforts are being considered on a case-by-case basis and diplomatic pressure will be applied where necessary.

The Home Minister further clarified that authorities are working to officially confirm Benazir's current location, verify allegations of multiple passports, and identify and seize illegal assets acquired both domestically and and abroad.
caption:
No leniency for fugitives. The government is working to bring former IGP Benazir Ahmed back from the UAE to face trial for corruption and disappearances.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated in the National Parliament on Tuesday that the government will show no leniency in bringing fugitive suspects, including Benazir Ahmed, back to Bangladesh to face trial.

The Home Minister noted that the government is coordinating with Interpol and various diplomatic missions to ensure the extradition of those currently residing abroad.

Benazir Ahmed, a former Inspector General of Police (IGP), served as the Dhaka Metropolitan Police Commissioner during the operations at Shapla Chattar. He faces allegations of enforced disappearances, corruption, and illegal asset accumulation.

Following the mass uprising of 2024, Benazir Ahmed left the country. Reports of his detention in Dubai have recently sparked demands in Parliament for his immediate return and legal action.

Members of Parliament from various parties, including Jamaat-e-Islami and BNP, called for strong measures to bring him back, with some proposing the creation of a special cell to identify and extradite fugitives.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kabir mentioned that extradition efforts are being considered on a case-by-case basis and diplomatic pressure will be applied where necessary.

The Home Minister further clarified that authorities are working to officially confirm Benazir's current location, verify allegations of multiple passports, and identify and seize illegal assets acquired both domestically and and abroad.

headline_marked: 34-run win: [[Bangladesh women reach Asia Cup semifinals]]
headline: 34-run win: Bangladesh women reach Asia Cup semifinals
summary: A strong bowling performance overcomes a poor batting display to secure a spot in the semis against India.
details: Bangladesh Women secured a 34-run victory over the UAE in their final Group B match of the Women’s Asia Cup T20 in Dubai, ensuring their place in the semifinals.
The victory makes them Group B runners-up, setting up a high-stakes clash with India on Thursday at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium.
Bangladesh struggled with the bat, falling to 55-6 in the 12th over. Captain Nigar Sultana Joty (23) and Juairiya Ferdous (16) provided early stability.
Experienced batter Sharmin Akhter Supta made a crucial impact in her tournament debut, scoring 38 off 31 balls to help the team post a total of 103-9.
The bowling attack dominated the UAE chase, with Marufa Akter taking two early wickets to put the hosts under immediate pressure.
Spinners Rabeya Khan (3-14) and Nahida Akter (2-18) tightened the grip, restricting the UAE to just 69-9 from their 20 overs.
Bangladesh will now face India in the first semifinal on Thursday, while Pakistan and Sri Lanka will compete in the other semifinal on Friday.
caption:
From 55-6 to the semifinals! 🇧🇩

Bangladesh women survive a batting collapse to beat UAE by 34 runs.

Bangladesh Women secured a 34-run victory over the UAE in their final Group B match of the Women’s Asia Cup T20 in Dubai, ensuring their place in the semifinals.

The victory makes them Group B runners-up, setting up a high-stakes clash with India on Thursday at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium.

Bangladesh struggled with the bat, falling to 55-6 in the 12th over. Captain Nigar Sultana Joty (23) and Juairiya Ferdous (16) provided early stability.

Experienced batter Sharmin Akhter Supta made a crucial impact in her tournament debut, scoring 38 off 31 balls to help the team post a total of 103-9.

The bowling attack dominated the UAE chase, with Marufa Akter taking two early wickets to put the hosts under immediate pressure.

Spinners Rabeya Khan (3-14) and Nahida Akter (2-18) tightened the grip, restricting the UAE to just 69-9 from their 20 overs.

Bangladesh will now face India in the first semifinal on Thursday, while Pakistan and Sri Lanka will compete in the other semifinal on Friday.
